aj: Heads-up — we've seen another flurry of flaky cards in eu-west-1 this morning. On-call keeps asking what to collect for triage. Can we make a tiny, copy-pasteable playbook for dmesg/journalctl/nvidia-smi collection so we stop losing context?

maria: Yep. I made a small script that grabs everything we need and timestamps it. Used by support and oncall. Paste below — drop into /tmp, run as root, it produces a tarball.

maria: ```
#!/bin/bash
OUT=/tmp/gpu-triage-$(hostname)-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).tgz
DIR=/tmp/gpu-triage-$(hostname)-$(date -u +%s)
mkdir -p "$DIR"
# kernel & driver logs
dmesg -T > "$DIR"/dmesg.txt
journalctl -k --no-pager > "$DIR"/journal-k.txt
journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced --no-pager > "$DIR"/journal-nvidia-persistenced.txt 2>/dev/null || true
# sys info
uname -a > "$DIR"/uname.txt
cat /proc/version > "$DIR"/proc_version.txt
modinfo nvidia > "$DIR"/modinfo-nvidia.txt 2>/dev/null || true
# pci + lspci
lspci -vvnn | grep -A 15 -i nvidia > "$DIR"/lspci-nvidia.txt 2>/dev/null || true
# nvml snapshot
nvidia-smi -q -x > "$DIR"/nvidia-smi-xml.txt || nvidia-smi -q > "$DIR"/nvidia-smi.txt
# topology and processes
nvidia-smi topo -m > "$DIR"/topo.txt 2>/dev/null || true
nvidia-smi pmon -c 1 > "$DIR"/pmon.txt 2>/dev/null || true
# any vendor logs
cp -r /var/log/nvidia* "$DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
# kubernetes context if present
if command -v kubectl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  kubectl get nodes -o wide > "$DIR"/kubectl-nodes.txt 2>/dev/null || true
  kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide > "$DIR"/kubectl-pods.txt 2>/dev/null || true
fi
# compress
tar czf "$OUT" -C "$(dirname "$DIR")" "$(basename "$DIR")"
echo "$OUT"
```

cheng: Add a Prometheus snapshot too — it helps correlate if this was a sustained temp spike or ECC counter climb. Example query we snapshot with grafana/api: gpu_temperature_celsius, dcgm_ecc_total, node_cpu_seconds_total (short window).

cheng: Also include the GPU UUID from nvidia-smi and the node serial from /sys/class/dmi/id/product_serial — we map failures to hardware replacements.

sasha: A couple of operational notes from recent postmortems: when you see Xid 31 or repeated ECC corrected errors in dmesg, immediate steps:
- cordon the node (kubectl cordon <node>)
- kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60 (adjust per infra)
- collect the tarball above before any driver restart
- if Xid continues after driver restart -> schedule a host reboot, but keep the tarball and nvml dump for support.

sasha: Also: Xid sample lines we look for in dmesg/journalctl: 
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, SM: 0x4100a05
[ 1234.567891] nvidia-uvm: PID 12345: page fault on 0x12345678, read
[ 1234.567892] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00 has fallen off the bus
```

maria: Also collect kernel oops if present: journalctl -k -b | grep -i -E "NVRM|Xid|GPU|oops" > filtered.txt — but keep the raw logs as well. We used to lose context by only copying filtered lines.

aj: Nice. Can we add a short checklist for oncall to paste into incident messages? Something like "what to paste into ticket" so support has all keys immediately.

maria: Sure — one-liner checklist:
- tarball path from script (attach)
- nvidia-smi -q top-level summary (driver / CUDA / GPU UUID)
- dmesg excerpt (first Xid and surrounding 20 lines)
- node name + cloud provider instance id + region
- pods evicted (kubectl get pods -o wide on that node)

maria: Example paste: 
```
node=ip-10-0-2-14.eu-west-1; tarball=/tmp/gpu-triage-ip-10-0-2-14-20260318T0630Z.tgz; driver=535.101; gpuUUID=GPU-abc123; first_Xid_line="NVRM: Xid (...)"; evicted_pods=5
```

cheng: Long-term: we should wire this script to our loghook collector so triage artefacts are auto-uploaded to S3 with metadata (node, gpu UUID, alarms). But until that lands, oncall runbook + script is low friction.

ops-bot: Reminder: please attach tarball to the #support-ticket when opening, use label "gpu-flake" and include the node tag.

aj: This is great. I'll drop the script into the ops repo and add a tiny runbook under oncall playbooks. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sasha: One more tip — if you suspect thermal issues, run `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu,fan.speed --format=csv -lms 1000` for a short period before draining to capture behavior.

maria: And if you see ECC multi-bit corrected errors creeping up, escalate to HW-replacement flow sooner rather than later — we've seen repeated corrected errors precede uncorrectable ones.

aj: Filing follow-ups: add prometheus snapshot script, add auto-upload later. Closing thread once runbook PR lands.
